speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I understand you are here because of vaginal bleeding after menopause and a mass in your pelvic area. To help me understand what is going on, could you tell me how long the bleeding has been occurring and if you have experienced any abdominal pain or bloating?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. I would like to request a transvaginal ultrasound and a pelvic CT scan to better characterize the adnexal mass and assess the endometrial thickness. Additionally, please check her CA-125 levels and complete blood count.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Transvaginal_Ultrasound
REQUEST TEST: CA-125
REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_CT_Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal test results are somewhat reassuring, but we need to rule out malignancy given the postmenopausal bleeding. Do you have any family history of breast, ovarian, or colon cancer?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol, retired school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that background information. To further evaluate the source of the bleeding and the nature of the mass, have you noticed any pelvic pressure, urinary frequency, or changes in your bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or flank pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the postmenopausal bleeding and adnexal mass, I need to evaluate the endometrium directly to rule out cancer. I will request an endometrial biopsy and a pelvic examination to assess the mass characteristics.

REQUEST TEST: Endometrial_Biopsy
REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Exam

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Endometrial_Biopsy: Well-differentiated adenocarcinoma; Pelvic_Exam: Vaginal atrophy, no active bleeding; A palpable left adnexal mass, non-tender, uterus non-enlarged

speaker: Doctor
text:
The endometrial biopsy confirms well-differentiated adenocarcinoma, which explains the postmenopausal bleeding. The adnexal mass may represent metastatic disease or a synchronous primary tumor, requiring further staging.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial Adenocarcinoma
